name: Wedge
purpose: The first play we install and the play we run when we need two yards. Every blocker takes the same man — whoever is over the center — and the whole line moves as one body. There is no hole to find and no read to make.

LE.rule: Close down to the tackle's hip, shoulder to shoulder. No daylight between you.

LT.rule: Close down to the guard's hip, shoulder to shoulder.

LG.rule: Close down to the center's hip, shoulder to shoulder. Get a hand on the center's back and stay attached.

C.rule: Snap it, then fire out low into whoever is closest. You are the point of the wedge — stay low and keep your feet moving.

RG.rule: Close down to the center's hip, shoulder to shoulder. Get a hand on the center's back and stay attached.

RT.rule: Close down to the guard's hip, shoulder to shoulder.

RE.rule: Close down to the tackle's hip, shoulder to shoulder. No daylight between you.

LW.rule: Step to the end's hip and push the back of the wedge. Never run around it.

RW.rule: Step to the end's hip and push the back of the wedge. Never run around it.

QB.rule: Take the snap, turn and hand the ball to the fullback at two yards, then get on the back of the wedge and push.

FB.rule: Two hands out, take the handoff and put your shoulder into the middle of the wedge. Keep your feet moving until the whistle.

coaching_points: The wedge only works if there are no gaps in it. Practice it standing still first, hip to hip, before anyone runs.
The fullback does not pick a hole. He runs into the back of the wedge and lets it move him.
If the wedge stops moving, the play is over. Teach the linemen to keep churning their feet after contact.
This is our short-yardage and goal-line play. Do not save it for emergencies — run it early so they have to respect it.
